# Preface {.unnumbered}

You have an idea for an app. Maybe it's a tool that would make your work easier, a service that fills a gap in the market, or a passion project you've been dreaming about for years.

In the past, turning that idea into reality meant one of three things: learn to code yourself (months or years of study), hire a development team (expensive and risky), or let the idea fade away.

That's no longer true.

AI coding assistants---Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenAI Codex CLI, and others---have fundamentally changed what's possible for non-technical people. You can now describe what you want in plain English and watch as working code appears in front of you. You can build real, functional applications---web services, iOS apps, Android apps---without writing a single line of code yourself.

This guide supports three command-line assistants from the start: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, and GitHub Copilot CLI. Most of the principles apply to all three. When commands differ, you'll see clear, tool-specific blocks so you can follow your chosen track.

## Choose Your CLI Assistant

Any of these tools will work for this guide. If you already pay for one, start there. Otherwise, pick whichever appeals to you—you can always switch later.

**Claude Code**
: Best if you already use Claude or want a purpose-built coding CLI with a native installer. Works on macOS and Linux, with Windows support via PowerShell/CMD or WSL.

**OpenAI Codex CLI**
: Best if you already have OpenAI access to Codex. Runs locally and is open source. Official support is macOS/Linux; Windows is experimental (WSL recommended).

**GitHub Copilot CLI**
: Best if you already pay for Copilot and want tight GitHub integration. It's in public preview and can be disabled by org policy; works on macOS, Linux, and Windows.

## Who This Guide Is For

This guide is for people who:

- Have an idea for a web or mobile application
- Have no coding experience (and don't want to become a programmer)
- Have a computer (examples use macOS, but concepts apply to any platform)
- Are willing to learn a few new concepts and tools

You don't need to understand programming languages, databases, or servers. You just need to be able to describe what you want clearly---a skill you already have.

## What You'll Learn

By the end of this guide, you'll know how to:

- Use a CLI assistant (Claude Code, Codex CLI, or Copilot CLI) to build and modify software projects
- Have productive conversations with AI about technical decisions
- Manage your code safely with version control
- Run and test your application locally
- Deploy your project so others can use it

## What You Won't Learn

This guide won't teach you to code. That's the point.

You'll learn enough vocabulary to have informed conversations with AI, but you won't need to understand the code it writes. Think of yourself as a product owner directing a development team---you decide *what* to build; your CLI assistant figures out *how* to build it.

## How to Use This Guide

Read the chapters in order. Each one builds on the previous, taking you from initial setup through to a deployed application.

When you see a boxed prompt like this:

:::{.callout-tip}
## Example Prompt
"Help me verify that everything is installed correctly."
:::

That's an example of what you might say to your CLI assistant. Feel free to adapt these prompts to your specific situation---they're starting points, not scripts.

Let's get started.

*This guide was written using Claude Code—using the very methods it teaches.*
